correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs stable maps without a hidden back-condition: an onto map to the three irreflexive markers forces all source markers, then the root, and rigidly fixes the markers. Each source graph vertex is forced into the corresponding target color class; relation preservation becomes precisely graph homomorphism. Conversely, a color-preserving surjective graph map extends markerwise. The finite-frame stable-formula criterion and finite model property of K4-stable extensions lift this equivalence to inclusion of full modal logics. Explicit closed walks give exactly the cycle surjections by vertex threshold, and K4 filtration gives the intersection statement. The accompanying script exhaustively checks 529 ordered small graph pairs and 21 cyclic witnesses; finite tests are only corroboration, not infinite proof. The hypotheses exclude empty color classes and nonconnected graphs where rigidity can fail.

originality.rationale: The highly relevant 2026 source proves a hardness reduction from surjective graph coloring and pairwise distinct cycle-axiomatized logics, but does not identify the entire inclusion poset, a strict descending cycle chain, or its meet. The 2016/2018 general stable-logic work proves the semantic transfer principle and constructs a different antichain, not this graph-order equivalence. The new work recovers fixed color classes from marker rigidity, uses finite model property to convert stable maps to logical implication, and determines the precise order and cyclic infimum. This assessment is a literature comparison, not a uniqueness certificate; the small source-to-claim distance remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The inclusion theorem reuses much of the 2026 gadget and older stable-formula machinery; the exact poset observation could be implicit in further unpublished notes or differently indexed discussions.
Semantic literature search does not establish absence of equivalent public or private work; no independent literature audit has occurred.

value.rationale: The order of infinitely many naturally parametrized modal extensions is completely characterized by a well-studied surjective graph-morphism order, yielding both comparability and incomparability from explicit graphs. In the especially motivated cycle family from the non-elementarity theorem, this gives a strict hierarchy of hard K4-stable logics whose exact infimum is K4; the previously known pairwise distinction alone provides neither the orientation of inclusion nor this limit. It is a structural classification and hierarchy result, not an arbitrary finite cutoff, code-only fact, or a marginal numerical increment.
